title: Virtual input-head motion under the suffix embedding
statement: Let $\alpha,x$ be bit strings, let $c$ be a configuration with $k$ work tapes on input $x$, and choose a direction $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$. At the head position $p$ of $c$, let $b$ be false when the one-cell marker tape has a $1$ at $p$ and true otherwise, and let $m$ be the virtual move determined by $b$, the symbol read by $c$, and $d$. Moving the head on the paired input $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ from the embedded position of $p$ by $m$ gives the embedding of the position reached by moving $c$'s input head by $d$ with clamping; moreover, as integers, $p+m$ equals that reached position.
hypotheses_covered: A configuration $c$ with $k$ work tapes on input $x$

replaced:
Let $\alpha$ be a bit string, let $c$ be a configuration of a machine with
$k$ work tapes on input $x$ whose input head is at position $p$, and let
$d \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$ be a direction.  Let $b$ be the marker-derived boundary
flag at $p$ (false exactly at $p = 0$) and let $m$ be the clamped virtual
move determined by $b$, the symbol under $c$'s input head, and $d$, which
suppresses stepping outward from a boundary blank.  Then moving the physical
head from the embedded position $2\abs{\alpha}+2+p$ on the self-delimiting
pairing $\langle \alpha, x\rangle$ by $m$ lands exactly on the embedding of
the position reached from $p$ by the clamped move in direction $d$, and, as
integers, $p + m$ equals that new virtual position.
